overview: After 1.Nc3 c5 2.b4 White offers a pawn on b4 as in the Sicilian Wing Gambit. If Black takes 2...cxb4, White gets time with 3.Nd5 or 3.Nb5 and usually follows with e4 and d4 for development. Rare and unpromising for White against sound play.

white_ideas.idea: Win time with Nd5 or Nb5 and then e4, d4
Open lines on the queenside with a3

black_ideas.idea: Take the pawn and hold it with ...e6 and ...Nc6
Develop calmly and return material if needed

typical_structures.structure: Open queenside after cxb4 with White using the central lead

character.notes: Unbalanced: White sacrifices a pawn early but Black can simplify.

gambit.notes: 2.b4 offers a wing pawn that Black can keep after 2...cxb4.

soundness.notes: Likely unsound if Black keeps the pawn; strong players seldom play it.

structure.notes: Queenside opens after the b-pawn exchange; the centre is undecided.

level.notes: Little theory and no deep plan; not a first-repertoire choice.

character.reason: A pawn is offered early on the wing.

soundness.reason: Black can keep the pawn and neutralise the compensation.

structure.reason: The b-file opens after cxb4 while the centre is unclear.

plans.reason: White uses b4 to gain time and open the wing.
